messages:
Marta: FYI I'm bringing up Newbridge LoRA on Helix-7B for customer Indigo. Dropped a tiny quick-eval (20 prompts) here: https://rwd.internal/evalpacks/newbridge/helix-quick.tar.gz. Seeing fragmented emails and token splits in outputs, can someone advise?
Ravi: Can you paste one failing case?
Marta: Example: prompt: "Please send report to ops+indigo@example.com" -> output: "Please send report to ops + indigo@ exa m ple .com". Repro:```bash
python infra/run_eval.py --model helix-7b --adapter newbridge-lora --quant int4 --inputs quick/edge_emails.json --out /tmp/newbridge.json
```
Tova: Reproduced with int4. Float16 baseline merges fine. Tokenizer warnings: "split_token_at_byte_boundary" logged 3x. :grimacing:
Arjun: Hunch: adapter was trained with a different BPE merge rule set -> introducing byte sequences that base tokenizer breaks under quantized decode. Also check kv_head_count mismatch warnings at merge time.
QA-Sam: Can you check whether sampling/top_p differences change the split frequency? Also add a metric: avg_token_split_rate per response. Set auto-fail if >0.01 for this pack.
Marta: Good call. I ran deterministic greedy and top-p=0.9 shots: greedy had 6/20 splits, top-p 11/20. Means decoder behavior interacts with the tokenization oddity.
Ravi: Two-pronged action: 1) verify adapter's tokenizer additions in adapter_config.json, 2) try remapping sequences to existing tokens at merge-time. If adapter specifies new tokens, we should register them on base before merging.
Arjun: Also check the adapter binary header: if n_kv_heads != base.n_kv_heads we silently pad weights causing attention misalignment under quantized kernels. That could amplify byte-boundary issues during decode. Our merge utility currently logs a warning but proceeds. Filing followup: ML-3490.
Marta: Minimal repro I used to inspect tokenizer:```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
base = Tokenizer.from_file('helix.tokenizer.json')
adapt = Tokenizer.from_file('newbridge.tokenizer.json')
for t in adapt.get_added_tokens():
    if t not in base.get_vocab():
        print('OOV', t)
```
Tova: I saw OOVs like `+indigo` and `ops+`. Options: (A) add those specials to base tokenizer at merge-time; (B) rewrite adapter to use canonical tokens `+` + localpart; (C) canonicalize emails in prompt preprocessor (ugly for customer). My vote short-term = (A) then issue a style request to adapter authors.
QA-Sam: Can we run a 3-way eval: float16 (merged), int8 (merged), int4 (merged) after adding the specials to the tokenizer? Want to confirm quant interaction disappears. Keep the input set identical and record split-rate + exact-match for email strings.
Ravi: I'll queue jobs. Using merge script with token registration flag:```bash
python tools/merge_lora.py --base helix-7b --lora newbridge --register-tokens adapters/newbridge/added_tokens.txt --out merged/newbridge-helix-merged.safetensors
```
ops-bot: queued job 2241 (float16), job 2242 (int8), job 2243 (int4)
Marta: Ran local patch: added `+indigo` and `ops+` to base tokenizer and remerged. Quick local eval (deterministic) -> int4 now 1/20 splits, int8 0/20, float16 0/20. Looks promising.
Arjun: We'll need a small change to merge utility to fail loudly when adapter.tokenizer has additions not present in base unless `--register-tokens` passed. Otherwise silent regressions happen. I'll PR the change.
QA-Sam: After PR/patch please run a focused smoke (20 inputs) that includes email-like tokens, currency, and unusual punctuation before we accept full quick-pack.
Marta: Will do. I'll push patch and post PR link in this thread. ETA ~90m.
ops-bot: created issue ML-3490: "Newbridge LoRA: tokenizer additions and kv-head mismatch causing token-splitting under quantized merges" assigned to Arjun and Marta.
